displayedInputs.question: Two circles lie outside regular hexagon \(ABCDEF.\) The first is tangent to \(\overline{AB},\) and the second is tangent to \(\overline{DE}.\) Both are tangent to lines \(BC\) and \(FA.\) What is the ratio of the area of the second circle to that of the first circle?
A palindrome between \(1000\) and \(10{,}000\) is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by \(7?\)

Seven distinct pieces of candy are to be distributed among three bags. The red bag and the blue bag must each receive at least one piece of candy; the white bag may remain empty. How many arrangements are possible?
The entries in a \(3 \times 3\) array include all the digits from \(1\) through \(9,\) arranged so that the entries in every row and column are in increasing order. How many such arrays are there?

A high school basketball game between the Raiders and Wildcats was tied at the end of the first quarter. The number of points scored by the Raiders in each of the four quarters formed an increasing geometric sequence, and the number of points scored by the Wildcats in each of the four quarters formed an increasing arithmetic sequence. At the end of the fourth quarter, the Raiders had won by one point. Neither team scored more than \(100\) points. What was the total number of points scored by the two teams in the first half?

Let \(a \gt 0,\) and let \(P(x)\) be a polynomial with integer coefficients such that \[ \begin{aligned} P(1) &= P(3) \\ &= P(5) = P(7) = a, \end{aligned} \] and \[ \begin{aligned} P(2)&=P(4)=P(6)\\ &=P(8)=-a. \end{aligned} \] What is the smallest possible value of \(a?\)

A ferry boat shuttles tourists to an island every hour starting at \(10\) am until its last trip, which starts at \(3\) pm. One day the boat captain notes that on the \(10\) am trip there were \(100\) tourists on the ferry boat, and that on each successive trip, the number of tourists was \(1\) fewer than on the previous trip. How many tourists did the ferry take to the island that day?
If \(x\lt0,\) then which of the following must be positive?

Halfway through a \(100\)-shot archery tournament, Chelsea leads by \(50\) points. For each shot a bullseye scores \(10\) points, with other possible scores being \(8,\) \(4,\) \(2,\) and \(0\) points. Chelsea always scores at least \(4\) points on each shot. If Chelsea’s next \(n\) shots are bullseyes she will be guaranteed victory. What is the minimum value for \(n?\)

A palindrome, such as \(83438,\) is a number that remains the same when its digits are reversed. The numbers \(x\) and \(x + 32\) are three-digit and four-digit palindromes, respectively. What is the sum of the digits of \(x?\)

Logan is constructing a scaled model of his town. The city’s water tower stands \(40\) meters high, and the top portion is a sphere that holds \(100{,}000\) liters of water. Logan’s miniature water tower holds \(0.1\) liters. How tall, in meters, should Logan make his tower?

Triangle \(ABC\) has \(AB=2 \cdot AC.\) Let \(D\) and \(E\) be on \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{BC},\) respectively, such that \(\angle BAE = \angle ACD.\) Let \(F\) be the intersection of segments \(AE\) and \(CD,\) and suppose that \(\triangle CFE\) is equilateral. What is \(\angle ACB?\)

A solid cube has side length \(3\) inches. A \(2\)-inch by \(2\)-inch square hole is cut into the center of each face. The edges of each cut are parallel to the edges of the cube, and each hole goes all the way through the cube. What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the remaining solid?
The first four terms of an arithmetic sequence are \(p,\) \(9,\) \(3p-q,\) and \(3p+q.\) What is the \(2010\)th term of this sequence?
The solution of the equation \(7^{x+7}=8^x\) can be expressed in the form \(x=\log_b 7^7.\) What is \(b?\)

In a magical swamp there are two species of talking amphibians: toads, whose statements are always true, and frogs, whose statements are always false. Four amphibians, Brian, Chris, LeRoy, and Mike live together in this swamp, and they make the following statements.

Brian: “Mike and I are different species.”

Chris: “LeRoy is a frog.”

LeRoy: “Chris is a frog.”

Mike: “Of the four of us, at least two are toads.”

How many of these four amphibians are frogs?
For how many integer values of \(k\) do the graphs of \(x^2+y^2=k^2\) and \(xy=k\) not intersect?
Nondegenerate \(\triangle ABC\) has integer side lengths, \(\overline{BD}\) is an angle bisector, \(AD = 3,\) and \(DC = 8.\) What is the smallest possible value of the perimeter?

A coin is altered so that the probability that it lands on heads is less than \(\dfrac12,\) and when the coin is flipped four times, the probability of an equal number of heads and tails is \(\dfrac{1}{6}.\) What is the probability that the coin lands on heads?

mappings.rationale: The target is the base in a logarithmic expression for the solution. It can be identified by rewriting the equation as one exponential or by taking logarithms and applying change of base.
mappings.answerReason: Dividing 7^(x+7)=8^x by 7^x gives 7^7=(8/7)^x. By the definition of logarithm, x=log_(8/7)(7^7), so b=8/7.

mappings.answerReason: If Mike were a toad, Brian's statement would contradict Brian's species in either case, so Mike is a frog. routes.label: Squares of the sum and difference

mappings.rationale: Real intersection feasibility produces inequalities in the integer parameter k. Counting the excluded integer values is route-neutral; square identities and a quadratic discriminant provide distinct feasibility methods.
mappings.answerReason: At an intersection, (x+y)^2=k^2+2k and (x-y)^2=k^2-2k. Conversely, nonnegative values on both right sides construct real x and y. Thus intersection occurs exactly for k<=-2, k=0, or k>=2. Only k=-1 and k=1 fail, giving two integer values.

mappings.rationale: The angle bisector fixes an integer side ratio. Nondegenerate triangle inequalities then bound its integer scale and determine the least perimeter.
mappings.answerReason: The angle bisector theorem gives AB:BC=3:8, so integer sides have AB=3t and BC=8t for a positive integer t, while AC=11. Triangle inequalities require 11t>11 and 3t+11>8t, hence 1<t<11/5. Thus t=2 and the perimeter is 6+16+11=33.

mappings.rationale: Exactly two heads in four independent flips gives a binomial probability equation for the unknown success probability. Its quadratic reduction can be solved by either formula or completing the square, with the stated bound selecting the root.
mappings.answerReason: Writing p for the head probability gives 6p^2(1-p)^2=1/6. Since 0<p<1/2, this implies p(1-p)=1/6. The quadratic roots are (3+sqrt(3))/6 and (3-sqrt(3))/6; only the latter is below 1/2.
